executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) in the Americas represents a Critical concern given its BSL-3 select agent status, ongoing animal-to-human spillover risk, and sustained transmission in wildlife and livestock. Mpox continues to circulate in the Americas as an Elevated BSL-3 threat, while dengue, measles, and pertussis show resurgent activity across multiple countries in the region. The convergence of southern hemisphere influenza season onset with RSV co-circulation further strains regional health systems.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) spillover risk in the Americas combined with simultaneous resurgence of dengue, measles, pertussis, and mpox creates a multi-threat burden requiring coordinated surveillance and rapid response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Sustained animal reservoir activity with documented human spillover risk
Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing spread
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential
Broad geographic spread across poultry, wild birds, and mammalian hosts in Americas
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interfaces; enforce PPE protocols for exposed workers; sequence all human cases; coordinate with FAO and OIE for animal health response

threats.name: Mpox
signals: Active transmission confirmed with dedicated PAHO update April 2026
BSL-3 select agent with sustained community spread
Ongoing cases reported across multiple Americas countries
Potential clade-related virulence concerns given global context
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and ring vaccination; expand laboratory diagnostic capacity; monitor for clade Ib importation into the region

threats.name: Dengue
signals: Epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating high transmission activity
Historically record-breaking dengue seasons in recent years across Latin America
Multiple serotypes likely co-circulating increasing severe dengue risk
Vector control capacity strained in endemic countries
threats.action: Intensify vector control and community engagement; ensure clinical capacity for severe dengue management; monitor serotype shifts

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza
signals: Southern hemisphere season start confirmed by PAHO alert April 2026
Previous alert December 2025 marking northern hemisphere season start indicating year-round burden
Simultaneous RSV co-circulation noted January 2026 increasing healthcare demand
Potential mismatch between circulating strains and vaccine composition
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination uptake ahead of southern hemisphere season peak; enhance syndromic surveillance; prepare ICU surge capacity

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained resurgence
Likely waning immunity and vaccine hesitancy driving transmission
Cases affecting infants and unvaccinated adults
Multi-country spread pattern consistent with epidemic wave
threats.action: Boost vaccination coverage including maternal Tdap programs; enhance neonatal protection protocols; conduct outbreak investigations in affected countries

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026
Epizootic activity in non-human primates signaling sylvatic cycle amplification
Risk of urban yellow fever reintroduction in unvaccinated populations
Aedes aegypti vector present across urban Americas
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk departments; ensure vaccine stockpile readiness; strengthen primate mortality surveillance as early warning

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 amid ongoing global resurgence
Importation risk from endemic regions with sub-optimal regional vaccination coverage
Pockets of unvaccinated communities identified in previous outbreak analyses
Risk of re-establishing endemic transmission in parts of the Americas
threats.action: Audit MMR vaccination coverage and conduct catch-up campaigns; strengthen port-of-entry surveillance; maintain case-based reporting systems

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025
Seasonal rodent population dynamics increasing human exposure risk
High case fatality rate (~35-40%) in confirmed pulmonary syndrome cases
Person-to-person transmission possible for Andes virus variant
threats.action: Issue public health advisories for rodent exposure prevention; enhance clinical recognition training; ensure rapid case confirmation at reference laboratories

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents are active in the Americas region. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) (Critical) continues sustained circulation in animal reservoirs with documented human spillover events, flagged in PAHO updates from November 2025 and March 2026, representing the highest-priority select agent threat given pandemic potential. Mpox virus (Monkeypox virus, BSL-3) is confirmed circulating in the Americas as of April 2026, representing an Elevated select agent threat requiring ongoing vaccination and containment measures. Both agents require BSL-3 laboratory handling and trigger enhanced biosafety and public health response protocols.
amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis with reduced macrolide susceptibility variants reported in some resurgence contexts, warranting surveillance for azithromycin treatment failures
Influenza antiviral resistance monitoring (oseltamivir) essential given H5N1 spillover cases and expanded antiviral use
No explicit AMR reports in provided surveillance titles, but concurrent multi-pathogen burden increases empiric antibiotic use pressure
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen epidemic activity across Americas region creating compounding healthcare system burden in 2025-2026
Back-to-back PAHO alerts for pertussis (December 2025 and March 2026) suggest a sustained epidemic wave not controlled by routine immunization
Southern hemisphere influenza season onset coinciding with residual RSV activity creates dual respiratory virus pressure on health systems
Two BSL-3 select agents (H5N1 and Mpox) concurrently active in Americas reflects elevated zoonotic and outbreak risk environment
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (February 2026) signals emerging pharmacovigilance threat alongside infectious disease burden
Chikungunya re-emergence alert in February 2026 combined with active dengue and yellow fever indicates expanding arboviral co-circulation zone
Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) highlights non-infectious public health chemical hazards requiring integrated surveillance
